questions.title: African Tourists, Rooibos Tea Prices, Currency Conversion and Travellers Data

subQuestions.questionText: The graph shows the number of people from four African countries (Malawi, Kenya, Namibia, Zambia) visiting South Africa (SA) for various reasons (Business, Holiday, Study). Name the country with the lowest number of people visiting SA for business. (Refer to the bar graph in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Kenya
Mark 1–2: Correct identification of country with lowest business visitors (Kenya = 141).
[Award 2 marks for the correct country]

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the countries that have the same number of people visiting SA for study purposes.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answers: Zambia and Malawi (both have 83 visitors for study purposes)
Mark 1–2: First correct country (Zambia or Malawi).
Mark 3: Second correct country.
[Award 3 marks: 2 for first correct country, 1 for second correct country]

subQuestions.questionText: Write down the country that has the greatest difference in people visiting SA for business, compared to those visiting SA for a holiday.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Malawi
Mark 1–2: Correct country (Malawi: Business = 6 069, Holiday = 178; difference = 5 891 — the greatest).
[Award 2 marks for the correct country]

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the total number of people visiting SA for study purposes.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Reading correct values from graph: 83 (Malawi) + 98 (Kenya) + 475 (Namibia) + 83 (Zambia)
Mark 2: Adding four correct values: $83 + 98 + 475 + 83$
Mark 3: Simplification: $= 739$ tourists
[Award 3 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: TABLE 1 shows prices, including VAT, of some rooibos tea items at a tourist shop. Item B is a Rooibos tea tin with 40 teabags priced at R50,00. Determine the price of ONE teabag if Samuel buys item B.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $\text{R}50{,}00 \div 40$
Mark 2: Simplification: $= \text{R}1{,}25$
OR
Mark 1: R1,25
Mark 2: $\text{R}1{,}25 \times 40 = \text{R}50$
[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Write, as a simplified ratio, the price of item D (Teapot, R185,00) to the price of item C (Rooibos Goddess tin with 50 pyramid teabags, R100,00).
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Reading correct values: 185 : 100
Mark 2: Values in correct order (D : C).
Mark 3: Simplification: $37 : 20$ OR $1 : 0{,}54$ OR $1{,}85 : 1$
[Award 3 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Samuel decided to purchase the following items for his wife: Teapot (R185,00); Rooibos Goddess tin with 50 pyramid teabags (R100,00); Gift bag (R16,00). Determine the total cost of his purchase.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Reading correct values: R185,00; R100,00; R16,00
Mark 2: Adding 3 correct values: $\text{R}185{,}00 + \text{R}100{,}00 + \text{R}16{,}00$
Mark 3: Simplification: $= \text{R}301{,}00$
[Award 3 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Tourists visiting South Africa need to convert their local currency to South African rand (ZAR). TABLE 2 shows the currency conversion factors for four African countries as at 27/04/2023. Write down the country whose currency has the same value as the SA rand.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Namibia
Mark 1–2: Correct country – the Namibian dollar (NAD) has a conversion factor of 1,000000 (1:1 with ZAR).
[Award 2 marks for the correct country]

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the currency that is stronger than the SA rand.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Zambian Kwacha (or Zambia / ZMW)
Mark 1–2: The currency where 1 ZMW = 1,029850 ZAR (i.e., 1 unit of foreign currency buys more than 1 ZAR).
[Award 2 marks for the correct currency]

subQuestions.questionText: Show how the Malawian kwacha of 0,017790 ZAR per unit was determined.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Dividing correct values: $\text{Malawian Kwacha} = \dfrac{1}{56{,}211355}$
Mark 2: Reading the correct value (56,211355) and obtaining $= 0{,}017790$
OR
Mark 1: Dividing correct values: $\dfrac{1}{0{,}017790}$
Mark 2: Calculating $= 56{,}211355$
[NPR]
[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: TABLE 3 shows data relating to the arrival, departure and transit of local and foreign travellers for three selected months. Total travellers for February 2022 = 1 105 685. Write, in words without numerals, the total number of travellers for February 2022.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: One million one hundred and five thousand six hundred and eighty-five.
Mark 1–2: Correct answer in words.
[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Determine missing value P (the total travellers for February 2021), given Local Travellers = 131 693 and Foreign Travellers = 254 139.
Calculate the increase in the number of local travellers from February 2021 to February 2022.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Subtracting correct values: $\text{Increase} = 359\,686 - 131\,693$
Mark 2: Simplification: $= 227\,993$
[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: State the month and the year in which the highest number of foreign travellers were in transit.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: February 2022 (or Feb '22 or 02/2022)
Mark 1: Correct month (February).
Mark 2: Correct year (2022).
[Foreign Travellers in Transit: Feb 2021 = 3 193; Jan 2022 = 11 463; Feb 2022 = 14 323 — Feb 2022 is highest]
[Award 2 marks]

questions.title: Credit Card Statement and Golf Club Income

subQuestions.questionText: Mr Warren Heyns received his Titanium credit card statement for his account at Standard Bank, dated 9 September 2023. Write down the amount paid to Standard Bank by Mr Heyns during September 2023. (Refer to ANNEXURE A in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: R2 000,00 (Accept –R2 000,00)
Mark 1–2: Correct amount from the credit card statement.
[NPU – No penalty for unit]
[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE valid reason why some numbers have been omitted from the account number.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: For security reasons (to prevent fraud / identity theft / unauthorised access to the account).
Mark 1–2: A valid security-related reason.
[Award 2 marks for a valid reason]

subQuestions.questionText: Outstanding authorisations refer to purchases that must still be finalised. Show, by means of calculations, how the amount of R8 323,78 for available money to spend was determined. (Credit limit = R20 000; Outstanding balance = R5 656,22; Outstanding authorisations = R6 020,00.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Reading 2 correct values from statement (R5 656,22 and R6 020,00).
Mark 2: Adding correct values: $\text{R}5\,656{,}22 + \text{R}6\,020{,}00 = \text{R}11\,676{,}22$
Mark 3: Subtracting from R20 000: $\text{Available} = \text{R}20\,000 - \text{R}11\,676{,}22 = \text{R}8\,323{,}78$
OR
$\text{R}20\,000 - \text{R}5\,656{,}22 - \text{R}6\,020{,}00 = \text{R}8\,323{,}78$
[Award 3 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: The amount paid to Caltex on 12/08/2023 was for 54,1365 litres of petrol. Calculate the price per litre of petrol on that particular day. (Total paid = R1 376,15.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Reading correct rand value: R1 376,15
Mark 2: Dividing by litres: $\text{Price/litre} = \dfrac{\text{R}1\,376{,}15}{54{,}1365 \text{ litres}}$
Mark 3: Simplification: $= \text{R}25{,}42$
[Award 3 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: The purchase at the Pro Shop on 24/08/2023 was for a Rovic RV2 golf push cart at a discounted price of R3 299,99. If a 17,5% discount was given on the price paid, calculate the original price of the Rovic RV2 golf push cart.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Calculate discounted percentage: $100\% - 17{,}5\% = 82{,}5\%$
Mark 2: Reading correct value: R3 299,99
Mark 3: Percentage calculation: $\text{Original price} = \dfrac{100}{82{,}5} \times \text{R}3\,299{,}99$
Mark 4: Simplification: $= \text{R}3\,999{,}99$
OR
Mark 1: $100\% - 17{,}5\% = 82{,}5\% = 0{,}825$
Mark 2–3: $\text{Original price} = \dfrac{\text{R}3\,299{,}99}{0{,}825}$
Mark 4: $= \text{R}3\,999{,}99$
[NPR]
[Award 4 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: TABLE 4 shows the actual and projected sources of income (in pounds £) of the Bay Golf Club based on previous trends in income for the years 2022 to 2026. Identify the source of income that is expected to generate the second highest income across the years.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Bar sales and Functions (Accept: Bar sales)
Mark 1–2: Reading correct item across all years (Membership fees is highest; Bar sales and Functions is second highest at £95 209 to £110 000).
[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: The ratio of the income for shop sales for 2023 and 2024 is given as 47 : 49. Determine missing value B (shop sales for 2024). Shop sales 2023 = 23 500.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Concept of ratio: $\dfrac{47}{23\,500} = \dfrac{49}{B}$
Mark 2: Reading 23 500.
Mark 3: Divide by 47: $B = \dfrac{23\,500 \times 49}{47}$
Mark 4: Simplification: $B = 24\,500$
OR
Mark 1: Total ratio = $47 + 49 = 96$
Mark 2: Reading 23 500.
Mark 3: Total income $= 23\,500 \times \dfrac{96}{47} = 48\,000$
Mark 4: $B = 48\,000 - 23\,500 = 24\,500$
[Award 4 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the percentage change in the total actual and projected sources of income from 2022 to 2025. (Total income 2022 = £396 453; Total income 2025 = £455 869.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Reading correct values: £396 453 and £455 869.
Mark 2: Difference in income: $\text{£}(455\,869 - 396\,453) = \text{£}59\,416$
Mark 3: % calculation: $\% \text{ change} = \dfrac{59\,416}{396\,453} \times 100\%$
Mark 4: Correct denominator (£396 453 — original/old value).
Mark 5: Simplification: $= 14{,}9868\ldots\% \approx 14{,}99\%$ OR $15\%$
OR via current percentage method:
$\dfrac{455\,869}{396\,453} \times 100\% = 114{,}99\%$; difference $= 114{,}99\% - 100\% = 14{,}99\%$
[Award 5 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: According to the website statista.com, the projected inflation rate for 2025 and 2026 will increase by 1,82% and 2% respectively. A club member stated that if the membership fees increased according to the projected inflation, the difference between the projected inflation value for 2026 and the projected table value for 2026 will be £16 611,31. Verify, with calculations, whether or not the club member's statement is VALID. (Membership fees 2024 = £257 460; Projected 2026 from table = £284 000.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Reading correct value: £257 460.
Mark 2: After year 1's inflation: $\dfrac{101{,}82}{100} \times \text{£}257\,460$ (or $\times 1{,}0182$)
Mark 3: Simplification: $= \text{£}262\,145{,}77$
Mark 4: After year 2's inflation: $\dfrac{102}{100} \times \text{£}262\,145{,}77 = \text{£}267\,388{,}69$
Mark 5: Subtracting values: $\text{Difference} = \text{£}284\,000 - \text{£}267\,388{,}69 = \text{£}16\,611{,}31$
Mark 6: Conclusion: Statement is VALID.
[Award 6 marks]

questions.title: School Teaching Periods and Learner Performance

subQuestions.questionText: Woodhill Senior Secondary School (SS) has a timetable with 40 periods per week. The number of periods per week allocated to staff members are listed (3, D, 26, 30, 32, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 34, 34, 35, 35, 35, 35, 35, 35, 35, 35, 36, 36, 36, 36, 37, 37, 37, 37, 37). Determine the number of staff members at Woodhill SS.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: 29
Mark 1–2: Correct count of staff members from the data.
[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Moloto Primary School (PS) has a timetable with 37 periods per week. The number of periods per week allocated to staff are: 10, 23, 25, 27, 27, 29, 29, 29, 29, 30, 30, 30, 30, 30, 31, 31, 31, 32, 32, 32, 34. Write down the modal number of periods per week for Moloto PS.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: 30 (mode — appears 5 times)
Mark 1–2: Correct mode.
[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate missing value D (the number of periods taught by the deputy principal at Woodhill SS — a Secondary School). Note: At a Secondary School, the deputy principal teaches $\dfrac{3}{5}$ of the total periods (40 per week).
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Reading correct fraction: $\dfrac{3}{5}$
Mark 2: Multiplying by 40: $D = \dfrac{3}{5} \times 40$
Mark 3: Simplification: $D = 24$ periods
OR via mean method:
$33 = \dfrac{933 + D}{29}$, so $D = 957 - 933 = 24$
OR
$D = 0{,}6 \times 40 = 24$
[Award 3 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Ina stated that since the calculated mean for Woodhill SS is 33, the median will be a better reflection of the average number of periods taught per staff member. Justify Ina's statement with calculations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1–2: Median = 35
Mark 3: Reason – Any ONE of the following:
• The median has half the staff above and half below.
• The outliers (e.g., low values like 3) affect the calculation of the mean, hence it is not a reliable average.
• More than 58,62% of staff have 35 periods or more.
[Award 3 marks: 2 for median, 1 for reason]
subQuestions.topic: Data Handling – Measures of Central Tendency

subQuestions.questionText: Determine, as a fraction, the probability of randomly selecting a staff member at Moloto PS who teaches 29 or more periods per week.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Numerator – 16 (staff with 29 or more periods).
Mark 2: Denominator – 21 (total staff at Moloto PS).
$P = \dfrac{16}{21}$
[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.label: 3.2.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText: TABLE 6A shows the percentages achieved in Term 1 by ten selected learners (A–J) for Task 1 and Task 2 in Mathematical Literacy. The performances are plotted on a graph on the answer sheet. Name the type of graph shown on the ANSWER SHEET.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Scatter plot (or scatter graph)
Mark 1–2: Correct identification of graph type.
[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.label: 3.2.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the range of the percentages achieved for Task 2.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Reading highest value: 81
Mark 2: Reading lowest value: 15
Mark 3: Simplification: $\text{Range} = 81 - 15 = 66$
[AO acceptable for full marks]
[Award 3 marks]

subQuestions.label: 3.2.1(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the learner whose marks for both tasks can be classified as an outlier. Give a reason for your answer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1–2: Correct learner – H (Task 1 = 22, Task 2 = 15)
Mark 3–4: Correct reason – Any ONE of the following:
• The marks for both Task 1 and Task 2 are much lower compared to the other learners.
• The learner failed while all the other learners passed.
[Award 4 marks: 2 for the correct learner, 2 for a valid reason]

subQuestions.questionText: The school's subject policy states that the difference between the mean of the two tasks should be below 15%. The mean for Task 1 is calculated as 66,7%. A teacher claimed that the difference in the mean mark for both tasks falls within the school's subject policy. Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether this teacher's claim is VALID. (Task 2 marks: 53, 69, 53, 49, 50, 47, 61, 15, 47, 81.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Correct concept of mean: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac{53+69+53+49+50+47+61+15+47+81}{10}$
Mark 2: Correct adding of values: $= \dfrac{525}{10}$
Mark 3: Mean Task 2: $= 52{,}5\%$
Mark 4: Simplification of difference: $\text{Difference} = 66{,}7 - 52{,}5 = 14{,}2$
Mark 5: Conclusion: VALID (since $14{,}2\% < 15\%$).
[Award 5 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: The achievements of two other selected learners, K and L, were added to TABLE 6A to create TABLE 6B. Learner K: Task 1 = 68, Task 2 = 40. Learner L: Task 1 = 88, Task 2 = 64. Use the ANSWER SHEET provided (where performances of Learners A to J for both tasks are plotted) to plot the results of Learner K and Learner L for both tasks. Clearly label the plotted points, K and L.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1–2: First point K plotted at (68; 40) and labelled.
Mark 3–4: Second point L plotted at (88; 64) and labelled.
[Award 4 marks: 2 per correctly plotted and labelled point]

questions.title: Church Fundraising Braai and Population Distribution

subQuestions.questionText: The fundraising committee of St Mark's Anglican Church is planning a braai. Each plate of food sold for R35 includes 1 chop, 1 boerewors, 1 salad and relish, 1 paper plate, 1 bread roll (sponsored). They bought 16,7 kg of chops (R149,95/kg) and 13 kg of boerewors (R99,99/kg) at a local butcher (enough for 200 plates). The fundraising committee negotiated a discount of 15% with the butcher on the total purchase made. Calculate the total amount the fundraising committee paid for the meat products at the local butcher.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Multiply correct values for chops: $\text{R}149{,}95 \times 16{,}7$
Mark 2: Multiply correct values for boerewors: $\text{R}99{,}99 \times 13$
Mark 3: Adding cost: $= \text{R}2\,504{,}165 + \text{R}1\,299{,}87$
Mark 4: Simplification: $= \text{R}3\,804{,}04$
Mark 5: Calculating 15% discount: $\dfrac{15}{100} \times \text{R}3\,804{,}04 = \text{R}570{,}61$
Mark 6: Subtracting correct values: $\text{R}3\,804{,}04 - \text{R}570{,}61$
Mark 7: Simplification: $= \text{R}3\,233{,}43$
[Award 7 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: The cost of the salad, relish, paper plates and charcoal is an additional R850,00. Calculate the cost price of ONE plate of food.
subQuestions.memoText:
CA from Question 4.1.1.
Mark 1: Adding value from Q4.1.1: $\text{R}3\,233{,}43 + \text{R}850$
Mark 2: Total: $= \text{R}4\,083{,}43$
Mark 3: Dividing by 200: $\text{Cost per plate} = \dfrac{\text{R}4\,083{,}43}{200}$
Mark 4: Simplification: $= \text{R}20{,}42$ (Accept R20,40)
[Award 4 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: The profit made from selling 200 plates of food was not sufficient. The fundraising committee still had a shortfall of R2 850,00 to buy the new generator. They decided to continue selling more plates of food to meet this shortfall. Determine, rounded to the nearest TEN, the total number of plates of food they had to sell in order to buy the new generator.
subQuestions.memoText:
CA from Question 4.1.2.
Mark 1: Subtracting values for profit per plate: $\text{R}35{,}00 - \text{R}20{,}42$
Mark 2: Profit per plate: $= \text{R}14{,}58$
Mark 3: Dividing by profit: $\text{Number of plates} = \dfrac{\text{R}2\,850{,}00}{\text{R}14{,}58}$
Mark 4: Simplification: $\approx 195{,}47$
Mark 5: Total plates: $200 + 195{,}47 = 395{,}47$
Mark 6: Rounding to nearest TEN: $\approx 400$ plates
[Award 6 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: The fundraising committee studied the estimated population distribution (as a percentage) per age group for the different race groups in South Africa. Write down the probability (as a percentage) of randomly selecting a white person from the white population in the 65+ age group. (Refer to ANNEXURE B in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: 15% (Accept range: 14,5 – 15,2)
Mark 1–2: Reading the correct value from the graph.
[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: It is given that the total number of people in the 55–64 age group is 4 052 572. The estimated total number of South Africans 15 years and older is 43 378 959. Give, rounded to THREE decimal places, the probability of randomly selecting a person in the 55–64 age group from the total number of South Africans, 15 years and older.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Numerator: 4 052 572
Mark 2: Denominator: 43 378 959
Mark 3: Simplification: $P = \dfrac{4\,052\,572}{43\,378\,959} = 0{,}0934\ldots$
Mark 4: Rounding to 3 decimal places: $= 0{,}093$ (or $9{,}342\%$)
[Award 4 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Identify which age group the fundraising committee should target for this fundraising venture. Give a reason for your answer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1–2: Correct age group: 25–34
Mark 3: Reason – The largest population is in this group (highest percentage of population).
[Award 3 marks: 2 for age group, 1 for reason]

questions.title: Personal Income Tax, Vehicle Finance and Hybrid Vehicle Sales

subQuestions.questionText: Malcolm, a 65-year-old consultant, earns an annual taxable income of R981 500 for the 2023/2024 tax year. He does not belong to a medical aid. State the total number of rebates Malcolm qualifies for. (Refer to TABLES 8 and 9 — Tax Table and Rebates Table.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: 2 (TWO)
Mark 1–2: Malcolm qualifies for the primary rebate (under 65) AND the secondary rebate (65 and older), since he is exactly 65. He does not qualify for the tertiary rebate (75 and older).
[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate Malcolm's monthly tax payable.
subQuestions.memoText:
CA from Question 5.1.1.
Mark 1: Reading correct tax bracket – 857 901 to 1 817 000.
Mark 2: Substituting R981 500: $\text{Tax} = \text{R}251\,258 + 41\% \times (\text{R}981\,500 - \text{R}857\,900)$
Mark 3: Amount before rebates: $= \text{R}251\,258 + 41\% \times \text{R}123\,600 = \text{R}251\,258 + \text{R}50\,676 = \text{R}301\,934$
Mark 4: Subtracting rebates: $\text{R}301\,934 - \text{R}17\,235 - \text{R}9\,444$
Mark 5: Simplification: $= \text{R}275\,255$
Mark 6: Dividing by 12: $\dfrac{\text{R}275\,255}{12}$
Mark 7: Simplification: $= \text{R}22\,937{,}92$ per month
[Award 7 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Malcolm is planning to buy a motor vehicle. The cash price of the motor vehicle is R334 000. He considers payment options to finance R300 000. Define the term interest rate in context.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Interest rate is the percentage of the total value you have to pay extra for taking the loan.
OR: Interest rate is a percentage charged on the loan taken to buy a motor vehicle.
Mark 1–2: Correct definition that includes the concept of percentage charged on a loan.
[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the difference between the monthly instalments of Option 1 (R6 115,47) and Option 2 (R5 498,19).
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Subtracting correct values: $\text{R}6\,115{,}47 - \text{R}5\,498{,}19$
Mark 2: Simplification: $= \text{R}617{,}28$
[AO acceptable]
[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate missing value X (Cost of loan for Option 1). You may use the formula: Cost of loan = Instalments × number of months − loan value. (Option 1: Monthly instalment = R6 115,47; Loan period = 6 years; Loan value = R300 000.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Substitution in bracket: $X = (\text{R}6\,115{,}47 \times 6 \times 12) - \text{R}300\,000$
Mark 2: Subtracting R300 000: $= \text{R}440\,313{,}84 - \text{R}300\,000$
Mark 3: Simplification: $X = \text{R}140\,313{,}84$
[AO acceptable]
[Award 3 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Determine missing value Y (Total payable for Option 2). You may use the formula: Total payable = Instalments × number of months + balloon payment. (Option 2: Monthly instalment = R5 498,19; Loan period = 73 months; Balloon = 20% of loan value, i.e. 20% of R300 000.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Reading correct values – R5 498,19 and R300 000.
Mark 2: Balloon payment: $20\% \times \text{R}300\,000 = \text{R}60\,000$
Mark 3: Multiplying by 72 months (instalment months — the 73rd payment is the balloon): $\text{R}5\,498{,}19 \times 72$
Mark 4: Adding balloon payment: $= \text{R}395\,869{,}68 + \text{R}60\,000$
Mark 5: Simplification: $Y = \text{R}455\,869{,}68$
[Award 5 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason why banks charge more interest on a personal loan compared to a motor vehicle loan.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: The vehicle serves as security (collateral) for the motor vehicle loan, while a personal loan is unsecured — so the bank takes on more risk and charges higher interest.
Mark 1–2: A valid reason about security/collateral.
[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Box and whisker plots summarise the percentage sales of the electrical vehicles (E) and plug-in hybrid vehicles (P) in South Africa. Write down the value of the lower quartile for the electrical vehicle (E) sales. (Refer to the box and whisker plot in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: 24
Mark 1–2: Reading the correct value (Q1) from the box and whisker plot for E.
[NPU]
[Award 2 marks]
subQuestions.topic: Data Handling – Box and Whisker Plots

subQuestions.questionText: An analyst stated that the interquartile range for the electrical vehicles was a quarter of the interquartile range of the plug-in hybrid vehicles. Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether or not the analyst's statement was VALID.
subQuestions.memoText:
CA from Question 5.3.1.
Mark 1: Using correct values for Electrical (Q3 ≈ 29; Q1 = 24): IQR = $29\% - 24\%$
Mark 2: Concept of IQR (Q3 − Q1).
Mark 3: Simplification: $\text{IQR}_E = 5\%$
Mark 4: Plug-in hybrid IQR: $24\% - 6\% = 18\%$
Mark 5: Quarter of plug-in IQR: $\dfrac{1}{4} \times 18\% = 4{,}5\% \neq 5\%$
OR comparison: $\dfrac{5}{18} \neq \dfrac{1}{4}$ (since $\dfrac{5}{18} \approx \dfrac{1}{3{,}6}$)
OR: Electric × 4 = $5\% \times 4 = 20\% \neq 18\%$
Mark 6: Conclusion: INVALID (the IQR for electrical is not exactly a quarter of the plug-in hybrid IQR).
[Award 6 marks]
subQuestions.topic: Data Handling – Interquartile Range and Verification
